name: Butcher
title: At the butcher (mesnica)
character: a friendly butcher at a small neighbourhood butcher shop (mesnica) in Ljubljana
setup: You are a friendly butcher at a small neighbourhood mesnica in Ljubljana. A foreigner who is just starting to learn Slovenian has come in to buy minced beef. They live here and want to practice.

objectives.label: Half a kilo of minced meat
objectives.hintEN: Order half a kilo of minced meat. Quantity genitive after 'pol kile': it's 'mletega mesa' (gen. sg.), not the nominative 'mleto meso'; and 'kile' is itself genitive after 'pol', not 'pol kila'.

objectives.label: Beef, please
objectives.hintEN: Specify beef, not pork (answering 'Goveje ali svinjsko?'). Neuter 'goveje' agrees with the dropped neuter noun 'meso' — common beginner errors are feminine 'goveja', masculine 'govej', or reaching for the animal noun 'govedo'.

objectives.label: Ask price
objectives.hintEN: Ask the price — a real exchange; the butcher answers with the cost. Just the question; do not bundle the goodbye onto it.

objectives.label: Pay & leave
objectives.hintEN: One-breath closing as you leave. Said on its own, not crammed onto the price question.

frames.imagePrompt: Viewpoint from inside the room looking toward the entrance: CUSTOMER stands in the open DOORWAY, framed by it, facing the viewer and waving as they step in over the threshold — the moment of arriving and greeting, seen from within the room they are entering.

A single portion of GROUND_MEAT sitting on the pan of the SCALE, the round dial's needle pointing straight to the halfway mark of its 0-to-1-kilogram face — unmistakably half a kilo. The weight 'half a kilo' is the point; nothing else on the scale.
A portion of GROUND_MEAT with a single COW standing right beside it — the meat is beef, from a cow, unmistakably not pork. The cow identifies the meat as beef; no other animal in the picture.
A single PRICE_TAG showing a large question mark '?' — the concept of asking how much it costs (a question, not a fixed price).

CUSTOMER stepping OUT through the DOORWAY, facing away with an over-the-shoulder wave — the moment of leaving and saying goodbye. The outward direction (leaving, not entering) is what makes this a farewell.
